text:
marie: Heads up — we've got a noisy inference fleet issue in cluster-prod-us-west. Several GPU-serving services are seeing retries and extremely uneven endpoint hits since ~13:07 UTC.

sam: seeing the same on my dashboards — p95 inference latency spiking and request_count concentrated on 2/8 endpoints for model-x.

lee: can you paste ipvs endpoint table? curious if kube-proxy is still doing round-robin or if conn tracking is skewing.

marie: sure. from node-gpu-03:```# ipvsadm -L -n --stats
TCP 10.0.42.10:443 rr
  -> 10.244.12.3:443           Masq    1      0          0          0
  -> 10.244.12.4:443           Masq    1      0       12000     950000
  -> 10.244.12.5:443           Masq    1      0      120000    11000000
  -> 10.244.12.6:443           Masq    1      0       80000     720000
```Looks like traffic concentrated on .5/.6, .3 barely any.

jake: any packet loss on the underlay? RDMA region has MTU 9000, CNI overlay is 1500, could be fragmentation on certain nodes.

marie: iperf between node-gpu-03 and node-gpu-07 shows higher retransmits when jumbo frames in path. also saw this in dmesg: "kernel: TCP: Possible reordering seen" and occasional "xsk: RX drop".

ops-sre: kube-proxy reported "sync failed, could not list services" earlier at 12:59, but restarted via daemonset auto-restart. logs show ipvs: "service sync timeout" and a flood of conntrack deletes.

sam: conntrack evictions would explain new flows hashed to a subset of endpoints — uneven load happens when connections get rebalanced while others stick. How's conntrack usage?

marie: conntrack count on node-gpu-03 at peak ~420k (limit 524k), on gpu-05 only 80k. evictions visible. snippet: ```# cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
420123
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
524288
```

lee: that is high. Also saw kube-proxy mode is ipvs with scheduler rr. But IPVS uses connection reuse flags; if conntrack removes entries mid-flight, new flows might hash to different backends but old ones still sticky — causing retries for the client and doubled requests.

jake: another datapoint: our RDMA-enabled nodes are split across two racks with different TOR firmware. TOR A has MTU 9000 path, TOR B had a recent QoS change that clamps to 1500 on some routes. So packets from certain pods take a path that hits smaller MTU and trigger fragmentation or drops.

marie: action plan suggestion: 1) temporarily cordon and drain the most affected nodes (gpu-03/05) from serving pool for model-x, 2) bump conntrack_max and enable conntrack hashing tweak, 3) run kube-proxy rollout with connreuse=false patch, 4) validate underlay MTU consistency and revert TOR QoS change.

ops-sre: doing 1 now on gpu-03 (cordon+drain). infra-bot: starting canary reroute.

infra-bot: Deploy: cordon/gpu-03 true, evicting pods, reason "investigating ipvs/retry spike".

sam: after cordon, p95 latency dropped ~30% and traffic rebalanced across remaining endpoints. Still seeing occasional 5xx retries for long-running streams.

lee: I opened a ticket with networking to check MTU asymmetry and TOR B config rollback. Also filing kernel bug suspicion for xsk RX drops.

marie: follow-ups: collect ipvs sync logs across all nodes, export conntrack dump for model-x namespace, and run a controlled traffic test with iperf + small/large MTU to reproduce. Also check whether autoscaler was overprovisioning endpoints and causing uneven kube-proxy maps.

jake: FYI, saving egress path logs — could be helpful: /var/log/rdma/rdma_stats.log and /var/log/kern.log around the window.

marie: thanks team. If networking confirms MTU mismatch, we'll schedule a rolling kube-proxy with connreuse=false and a small kernel param change to reduce conntrack churn. Will keep updates here. :white_check_mark:
